lines.t: Hi, Omar. Do you have a minute? We need to organise the team meeting for next week.
Of course. The last one was on a Monday, but several people couldn't come. How about Wednesday?
Wednesday is better for me, too. Shall we say ten o'clock in the morning?
Ten is fine. But I have to leave at eleven thirty for a visit to a client, so the meeting should not be longer than ninety minutes.
Right. I think an hour will be enough. Which room should we use?
The big meeting room is already booked. We could use the small one on the third floor, but it only has eight chairs.
There are nine of us, so that is a problem. Perhaps we can borrow a chair from the office next door.
Good idea. And what is on the agenda?
First, the budget for next year. Then, the new customer service system. And finally, the holiday plan for the summer.
Should we send the agenda in advance?
Yes, I will email it tomorrow morning. Could you bring the printed budget report? Ten copies, please.
No problem. Do we need to order coffee and biscuits?
Just coffee, I think. I will ask the kitchen.

qs.why: قالت: There are nine of us.

title: A guide to a university campus

lines.t: Hello, new students, and welcome to Hillside University. My name is Jake, and I am a third-year student. Let me show you the most important places on campus.
We are standing in front of the Main Building. This is where you will find the registration office, which is open from nine to four, Monday to Friday.
You need to go there to collect your student card.
Behind it, you can see the Central Library. It has four floors, and the top floor is silent. During exams, it stays open twenty-four hours a day.
On the right, the glass building is the Science Centre, with laboratories and lecture halls. Most first-year science classes are held here.
If you walk down the hill, you will reach the Student Hub. It has a cafe, a small shop and a room where you can relax between classes.
A lunch there costs about five dollars.
The sports hall is next to the car park. Membership is free for students, and it has a gym and a swimming pool.
Finally, remember that the campus bus runs every ten minutes from the main gate to the student housing. It is free if you show your card.
Now, let's go and see the library.

qs.why: قال إنه طالب في السنة الثالثة.

title: A talk on transparency in local government

lines.t: Good afternoon. Today, I would like to talk about transparency in local government, and why it matters for ordinary citizens.
Transparency means that the public can see how decisions are made and how public money is spent.
In a transparent town, the council publishes its budget, its contracts and the minutes of its meetings, so that anyone can read them.
Why is this important? There are three main reasons. First, transparency helps to prevent corruption.
When officials know that people can check their decisions, they are less likely to misuse public money.
Second, it builds trust. Citizens are more willing to pay taxes and to follow rules when they understand what happens to their money.
Third, it improves services.
When residents can see which roads are repaired and which schools are built, they can say what they need, and the council can plan better.
How can a town become more transparent? Some councils publish contracts on a website, where citizens can search them.
Others hold open meetings, or let people ask questions online. A simple measure is to publish every contract above a certain value, for example ten thousand pounds.
Of course, transparency is not enough on its own. People also need to know their rights, and the authorities must answer their questions within a reasonable time.
Thank you.

qs.q: What does transparency mean in the talk?
o: Public access to how decisions are made and money is spent
qs.why: أن يرى الناس كيف تُتخذ القرارات وتُنفق الأموال.

qs.q: The council publishes its budget, its contracts and the ___ of its meetings.

The speaker thinks transparency alone is enough.

title: A phone call to a bank about a new card

lines.t: Good morning, Northern Bank. This is Helen. How can I help?
Good morning. I would like to order a new debit card, please. My old one stopped working last week.
I am sorry about that. For security, I need to ask a few questions. Can you give me your full name and date of birth?
Yes. It is Rami Haddad, and my birth date is the twelfth of March, nineteen ninety-eight.
Thank you. And the first line of your address?
Fourteen Elm Road.
That is correct. Did you lose the card, or is it just damaged?
It is damaged. The chip is broken, so the machines don't read it.
In that case, there is no charge for the replacement. The new card will arrive in five working days.
Can I collect it from the branch instead? I am often out during the day.
Yes, you can. Which branch is nearest to you?
The one in Market Street.
I will arrange that. Please remember to bring your passport when you collect the card.
Will I keep the same PIN?
No, you will get a new one by post, in a separate letter.

qs.why: ولد في الثاني عشر من مارس 1998.

qs.q: The first line of his address is ___ Elm Road.

lines.t: Okay, we have collected all the answers. Let's look at the results of our survey about student transport. Maya, how many people replied?
One hundred and twenty. That is more than we expected. We only planned for a hundred.
And what were the main findings, Maya?
Well, forty-five percent of the students come to campus by bus. Thirty percent walk, and only fifteen percent come by car.
I am surprised that so few use bicycles.
Only ten percent do. Many said that the roads aren't safe, and there is nowhere to park a bike.
That could be an interesting recommendation. We could suggest more bicycle racks near the library.
Yes. What about the bus? Did people complain?
Quite a lot. Sixty students said that the buses are too crowded in the morning, and some mentioned that they wait more than twenty minutes.
Then we should include a graph about waiting times. Leo, can you make it?
Sure, I will do it tonight. When is the report due?
Next Friday. So let's meet again on Monday to check everything.
I will write the introduction and the conclusion by then.
